q-72120.name: Question 1
q-72120.problem: Which of the following is a type II region in two-dimensional space?
q-72120.worked_solution:
A type II region can be written as

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,a\le y\le b,\,g(y)\le x\le f(y)\},
$$

where $f$ and $g$ are continuous functions.

A type II region has the property that a horizontal line drawn through the region intersects the region in a single interval only.

Among the given options, the only type II region is the following.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14150788/assets/e472070f17c47e78024217ed750690b88de87f3849818368dda1dde5d91d90d4.png)

q-72185.name: Question 2
q-72185.problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the finite region inside the circumference ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1?$

I. It is a type I region

II. It is a type II region

III. It's neither a type I nor a type II region
q-72185.worked_solution:
First, notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1\, & ⟹\,x=\pm \sqrt{1-{y}^{2}} \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1\, & ⟹\,y=\pm \sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14150788/assets/0960063edcce8ccd55dc2f77147c4a4982645c180e8b998d7e520c65131ea045.png)

We have the following:

- Any vertical line through the region intersects it on a single interval. Furthermore, we can represent our region as

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,-\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}\le y\le \sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}\}.
$$

So, this is a type I region.

- Any horizontal line through the region intersects it on a single interval. Furthermore, we can represent our region as

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le y\le 1,\,-\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}\le x\le \sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}\}.
$$

So, this is a type II region.

Therefore, only statements I and II are true.

We have the following:

  • Any horizontal line through the region intersects it on a single interval. Furthermore, we can represent our region as D={(x,y):−1≤y≤1,−1−y2≤x≤1−y2}. So, this is a type II region.

Therefore, only statements I and II are true.

q-72345.name: Question 4
q-72345.problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the finite region bounded between the line $y=x$ and the curve $y={x}^{3},$ in the first quadrant?

I. It is a type I region

II. It is a type II region

III. It's neither a type I nor a type II region
q-72345.worked_solution:
First, notice that

$$
y={x}^{3}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt[3]{y}.
$$

Now, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14150788/assets/1d1c1cbe30e6f612f824adc76d712a98194ffccc5edefc11cccdaf07204513ba.png)

We have the following:

- Any vertical line through the region intersects it on a single interval. Furthermore, we can represent our region as

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{3}\le y\le x\}.
$$

So, this is a type I region.

- Any horizontal line through the region intersects it on a single interval. Furthermore, we can represent our region as

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,y\le x\le \sqrt[3]{y}\}.
$$

So, this is a type II region.

Therefore, only statements I and II are true.

Therefore, only statements I and II are true.
